title: Verbs Followed by Prepositions
summary: Learn common verb-preposition combinations such as gostar de, precisar de, depender de, and assistir a.

sections.heading: De after common verbs
sections.body: Many frequent verbs require **de** before their complement. When an article follows, de contracts with it: do, da, dos, das.

sections.heading: A after movement, help, and watching
sections.body: Several verbs take **a**, including **assistir a** in the sense of watching, **responder a**, **obedecer a**, and many destination expressions.

examples.en: I replied to the message early.

sections.heading: Em, com, and por
sections.body: Other verbs select **em**, **com**, or **por**. These combinations are often lexical, so learn them as chunks rather than translating word for word.

keyPoints: Verb-preposition combinations are called regência verbal.
Do not translate English prepositions mechanically.
Contractions are required when a preposition meets an article.
Learn frequent combinations as complete phrases.

commonMistakes.note: In standard Portuguese, assistir = watch takes a.
Acreditar requires em before a person or idea.
